header_sentences: See Faith alone, Good of Faith, and Historical Faith; and also see Acknowledge, Believe, Fruit, Ground, Justify, Lamp, Moon, Peter, and Reuben.

contexts.text: The fourth state is when he is affected with love, and illuminated with faith.
The sixth state is when from faith and thence from love, he speaks truths and does goods.
The very essence and life of faith is the Lord alone...

The progress of faith with those who are being created anew... They receive life from the Lord through faith; first through the faith of the memory, which is scientific faith; next through faith in the understanding, which is intellectual faith; and afterwards through faith in the heart, which is the faith of love, or saving faith. (These kinds of faith here represented.)
Love and faith in the internal man are circumstanced as are heat and light in the external corporeal man...
The Lord's mercy affects... the understanding with truth or faith.
Great luminaries = love and faith.
Afterwards, faith is called a lesser luminary... and it is said of faith that it shall rule by night.
Scarcely any love, and therefore scarcely any faith. Signified.
The celestial Angels do not know what faith is, except that which is of love.
Love and faith can never be separated...

Thus they who are in love are also in faith... But the life of faith without love is circumstanced as is the light of the sun without heat... But faith from love is circumstanced as is the light of the sun in the time of spring... No faith, and faith without love, are also compared by the Lord to winter...
Those who say they have faith, but live otherwise...

They who have separated faith from love, do not even know what faith is. When they are in the idea of faith, some know no otherwise than that it is mere thought; some that it is thought directed to the Lord; a few, that it is the doctrine of faith. But faith is not only the Knowledge of all things embraced in the doctrine of faith, and the acknowledgement of these things, but it is especially obedience to all things which it teaches... If a man is not in the love of the Lord and in the love of the neighbour, he is not in faith.
Now, when man is vivified by love and faith...
The things which are from the Lord have life in themselves, because they have faith in Him.
Scientifics animated by faith from the Lord. Signified.
The mysteries of faith. AC 80. AC 126. AC 206. AC 233. AC 298. AC 302. AC 308.
Multiplication is predicated of the things of faith.
It is the fifth state in which man speaks from faith, which is of the understanding... AC 52:end.
Faith which is of the understanding is called His image.
As the most ancients called the conjunction of... faith and love a marriage...
As faith is being conjoined with love...
So that he may have an undoubting faith.
Now the things of faith make one with those of love. Signified. AC 63.
Adam in paradise = the faith in the Lord of the Most Ancient Church. Signified.
Abraham = saving faith.
Faith is signified by the tree of knowledge.
A spiritual man acknowledges truth and good... from faith; and from this he also acts... A celestial man... acknowledges no faith but that which is from love; and from this he also acts. AC 459.
Under Believe, see this reference. AC 231. AC 1608:2. AC 1812. AC 3394:3. AC 3865:2. AC 8240. AC 9239. DFaith 10. DFaith 36. AE 328:6.
To scrutinize the things of faith in the Lord, whether they were so. Treated of. AC 204.
Thus faith, that is, all wisdom and intelligence, would perish.
But with this man... that is, his descendants, the midst of the garden was faith.
(The members of the Most Ancient Church) were not allowed to think from sensuous and scientific things about anything that was of faith...

The more interiorly celestial of the celestial Angels do not admit of the mention of faith... and if it is mentioned by others, instead of faith they perceive love, with a difference known only to themselves; thus whatever is of faith they derive from love and charity; still less can they endure to hear anything rational, and least of all anything scientific about faith... and therefore when anything is said about faith, they merely reply that it is so, or that it is not so, because they perceive from the Lord. Signified. AC 6435, References. AC 7877:2. HH 270:2. DLW 427:2.
For to reason about faith is to doubt and deny.
The seed of the woman = faith in the Lord. (Explained.)
The Lord alone gives faith, and thus is faith.
To provide against his having power to enter into any arcanum of faith. Signified.

Faith or truth is of the understanding; from love or good they perceived what is of faith or what is of truth... But with the postdiluvians, and with those who live now, there is no love... but still there can exist faith, or the understanding of truth; and from faith or the understanding of truth they can be brought to a kind of charity...
The Most Ancient Church through love had faith in the Lord...
As it was faith through which charity was afterwards to be implanted...

The Most Ancient Church acknowledged no other faith than that which was of love to the Lord and towards the neighbour; through this love from the Lord they had faith, or the perception of all things which belonged to faith; and therefore they were unwilling to mention faith, lest it should be separated from love. Signified. AC 393. AC 597:end. AC 895. AC 1121.
Under Cain, see this reference. AE 427:6.
What is it that is done by faith, or knowledge, Knowledge, and the doctrine of faith, but that man does as it teaches The primary thing it teaches is charity.
Faith, too, is celestial when it is from love.
When men are thinking about a single article of faith, they make it the principal thing. (Hence heresy.)

They made no distinction between love which is of the will, and faith which is of the understanding; because love was everything, and faith was of love. But after faith was separated from love, as was the case with those who were called Cain, the will had no longer any rule; but as... faith reigned in that mind instead of love, it is said that he dwelt towards the east of Eden; for faith was distinguished, or had a mark set on it, that it might be preserved for the use of mankind.
Lamech, who was the sixth in order, altogether denied even faith.
It belongs to faith to understand not only what is true, but also what is good; the Knowledges of faith involve both; but to be such as faith teaches is celestial.
Twelve = faith, or the things which are of love and of faith thence in one complex.
Noah (also) = the faith of that Church, which was the faith of charity. So the Lord foresaw, that the human race could be saved through the faith of charity.
As love is the containant of faith, and faith is the containant of the Knowledges of faith.
Faith is only the form of love... and the faith is thence formed according to the quality of the love or charity.

To see = to understand, and to have faith. (AC 9165, References.) To know Truths, to acknowledge Truths, and to have faith in Truths, are three completely different things. To know is the first of regeneration, to acknowledge is the second, and to have faith is the third... Infidels can acknowledge, and when in certain states, can from zeal preach, confirm, and persuade; but none can have faith except the faithful. They who have faith know, acknowledge, and believe; they have charity; they have conscience; and therefore faith can never be predicated, that is, it cannot be said of anyone that he has faith, unless he is of this character. Merely to know what is of faith, belongs to the memory without the consent of its Rational; to acknowledge what is of faith, is a certain Rational consenting, being induced to do so by certain causes, and for the sake of certain ends; but to have faith is of the conscience, that is, of the Lord operating through the conscience... In the other life, many who only know (and also many who only acknowledge) are in Hell... But they who have had faith are all in Heaven.
By faith... is meant charity from which is faith; for no other faith exists, which is faith, except the faith of charity.
When on account of the voluntary proprium of man, the faith of charity does not appear. Signified.
Wine = the faith (which is derived from charity), and all things which are of faith... He drank of the wine = that he wanted to investigate the things that are of faith... by reasonings. Illustrated.
For faith is no other than of charity; and, essentially, is charity itself... AC 2034.
It is as impossible to acquire faith from these (reasonings) as...

As they are devoid of charity, they do not know what faith is. When asked, they can only reply that it is a kind of thought; some, that it is confidence; others, that it is the Knowledges of faith; a few, that it is a life according to Knowledges; and scarcely any that it is the life of charity or of mutual love.
Faith is the acknowledgement of those things which belong to faith; and the acknowledgement is never external but internal, and is the operation of the Lord alone through the charity with the man.

They do not know that love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour are faith itself; and that the Knowledges which they call faith have no end but (the reception of these loves); and that this is the faith which saves.
The first-born of every Church, in the internal sense, is faith.
According to their languages = according to the differences as to faith.
A good Spirit is known not only as to the goodness, but also as to the faith in which he is. AC 1389.
That heavenly things would be given to those who have faith in the Lord. Signified. AC 1608. AC 1986. AC 2027.
There are two things in the internal man, love and faith; and these two constitute a one when faith is from love.
Faith and the things of faith are nothing but truths. AC 1685.

The conjunction of men with the Lord is effected through... the implantation of faith in love. Unless faith is implanted in love; that is, unless a man, through the things which are of faith, receives the life of faith, that is, charity, there is no conjunction.

By the faith which is the internal of the Church is meant no other than that which is of love and charity; that is, which is from love or charity. In a general sense, faith is everything doctrinal of the Church; but what is doctrinal separated from love or charity never makes the internal of the Church... That (the former) is the faith which is the internal of the Church, may be evident from this fact alone, that he who has the life of charity knows all things of faith.
When there is no faith, that is, no charity...
The Celestial Spiritual... is faith in which there is charity, or faith which is generated from charity. AC 2184:4.
They who learn Knowledges in order to be perfected in the faith of love are in the use of all uses...
When faith or truth is treated of... God is mentioned.
Conjunction with those who have faith in Him. Signified. AC 2034. AC 2085.

Generations = the things which are generated and born from charity, that is, all things of faith; or, what is the same, all those who are regenerated by the Lord, thus in whom there is the faith of charity.
(House = the Celestial of faith; temple = the truth of faith.)

Seed, here, = those who have the faith of love, that is, love to the Lord, thus the celestial... Whereas they who have the faith of charity, that is, charity towards the neighbour, thus the spiritual... are signified by Ishmael.

The saying that those are saved who have faith is true, but by faith nothing else is meant in the Word than love to the Lord and charity towards the neighbour, thus the life thence. The doctrinal things and dogmas of faith are not faith, but of faith...
Holiness is never predicated... of faith, except in the proportion that there are love and charity in the truths of faith. AC 2343:end.
In the good of charity with man are... all things of his faith.
The love of the world is diametrically opposite to the spiritual things of faith; and the love of self, to the celestial things of love.
The essential things of faith, being necessary to salvation, are expressed in the letter such as they are in the internal sense.

Many say that man is saved by faith; or, as they say, if only he has faith; but most of them do not know what faith is; some suppose that it is mere thought; some, that it is the acknowledgement of something that is to be believed; others, that it is the whole doctrine of faith which is to be believed... Thus they err in the mere Knowledge of what faith is.

It is this heavenly life which is regarded by all those things which are called faith; and it is procured by all things of faith. Hence it may be evident what faith is, namely, that it is charity; for to this lead all things which are called the doctrines of faith...
Faith from charity is like the light in the time of spring and summer, by which all things germinate and flourish; (for) love and charity is celestial flame, and faith is the spiritual light thence.
Judgment = faith; justice, love... Judgment precedes, because love comes through faith; but when justice precedes, it = that faith is from love. AC 2826:9.
I will betroth thee unto Me in faith ()... Both (justice and judgment) are here called faith, or fidelity.
The desolation of faith, which is effected by falsities. Treated of.
They do not even know that the fundamental of faith is love to the Lord and charity towards the neighbour.
Hence, faith itself, in the internal sense, is nothing else than charity.

To see = to have faith... The reason it here = conscience, is that those who have faith have conscience too; the former is inseparable from the latter, and in fact so inseparable, that whether you say faith or conscience is all the same. By faith is meant the faith by which comes charity, and which is from charity, thus is charity itself; for faith without charity is no faith.
Evening = the state of the Church before the last, when there begins to be no faith.
As the conjunction of the Lord with mankind is effected through love and charity, and the faith thence...

For the good of charity is the very ground of the seeds of faith... and therefore in proportion as a man is in... charity, he is in faith, especially in this principal of faith, that all salvation is from the Lord.
That no one can have faith unless he is in charity, is evident from  etc.
From these passages it is evident that love to the Lord, and charity towards the neighbour, is the life of faith. Explained.
Here is described the first state of the vastated Church, when there begins to be no faith, because no charity.

They may suppose that they can easily receive faith (after death), when they see that the Lord rules the universal Heaven... but it is as far from being possible for the evil to receive faith... as Hell is from Heaven...
That they are saved who are in the affection of truth, that is, who are in faith, provided it is the faith of good. Signified. AC 2442.
The spiritual things of faith are all the truths which are from good.
The good of doctrine is love and charity; the truth of doctrine is faith.
Those think from the affirmative who believe that they are truths because the Lord says so in the Word, thus who have faith in the Lord.
They who are in love to the Lord and charity towards the neighbour are able to... have faith in the Word; but not they who are in the love of self and of the world...
In (this gentile) there was the mercy which is of love, and in his ignorance there was innocence; and when these are present, all things of faith are received as it were spontaneously.
Persuasive light... induces a faith of falsity by truths, and a faith of truth by falsities.
The eye = the understanding, the Spiritual of which is faith. AC 2701:3.
They apprehended with the understanding and had faith, which is to see with the eyes.
The sight of the understanding is from the light of Heaven flowing into those things which are of the light of the world; but the sight of faith is from the light of Heaven.
Water = the Spiritual of faith; and spirit. its Celestial.
It is this union (of the Divine and the Human) by which they can be saved who have the faith of charity in Him. AC 2836:end.
The confirmation of an idea by many things causes... that faith can be insinuated into it.
Seed = the faith of charity, or... those who are in the faith of charity, that is, the spiritual.
No others are in the faith of charity than they who are within the Church; for the faith of charity is the truth of doctrine adjoined to the good of life.

The truth of doctrine, or faith, is insinuated by an external way, and is carried into the memory; and is called forth thence by the Lord in its own time and order, and is conjoined with the affection of good. This is effected in the freedom of man... Such is the insemination and inrooting of faith: whatever is effected in freedom is conjoined...
(Thus) the truth of doctrine or faith can only be received by the affection of it.
The reception of faith with those who are of the Church. Treated of. AC 2913:3.
When there is no longer any faith, that is (or because there is no) charity. AC 2908. AC 2909:3. AC 2910:2. AC 3398:4. AC 3652.
What is obscure of faith. Signified. AC 2945. AC 2946.
A city = faith; and its gates, doctrinal things; because these introduce to faith.
They are here said to be vivified because they are in the progression of receiving faith; for from faith, namely, from its good, they receive life, of which this is the only source.

Quite different is the case with the Churches which say that faith is the essential of the Church... They say, indeed, that the veriest faith which saves is trust, but this trust is possible only in the good of life...

In the proper sense, Truth signifies the same as faith; in the Hebrew language, too, faith is expressed by such a word; so that that which is called Truth in the Old Testament is called faith in the New Testament; and therefore it has been so often said that truth is of faith... But, in the internal sense, faith is nothing but charity; and there is no faith except by love. References... For all faith is from charity...
Unless truth is learned from affection, thus in freedom, it is not... exalted towards the interiors, and there made faith.

Such is the rooting of faith, or of the truth which is of faith, that unless it is coupled with good in the Rational, the truth of faith never receives any life, nor is any fruit produced thence; for that which is called the fruit of faith is the fruit of the good which is of love and charity through the truth which is of faith.
When the truth of faith is received by the will... faith is of charity, or as to life is charity itself.
Unless the truth of faith... is received by the good of love... it is not faith.
Causes... the truth (in the natural man) to receive the rays of light, that is, faith.
Seed = those who are in charity through faith, that is, the spiritual.

In order that the spiritual man may have the truth of faith, or faith, it must come from the new understanding with which he is endowed by the Lord, and the new understanding must have its light from the new will.
They who are of the Spiritual Church are in faith, namely, in its good and truth... The truth which the spiritual have is that of faith, so far as this is doctrine concerning charity.
See Doctrine. AC 3242. AC 3325:11. AC 3419:3. AC 5402:2. AC 5637:end. AC 8980. AC 9918. LJ 38. DP 101:end. TCR 245.

No one is admitted into the Lord's Kingdom unless he is in the good of faith... Still, they who are in the truth of faith, that is, who profess faith, and call it the essential thing... and yet are in the good of life... are in the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom.
The Lord's Spiritual Kingdom in the Heavens is... various as to the things which are of faith.
The struggle as to whether... charity which is of good or faith which is of truth is the prior. Treated of.
To look from faith, and not from love and charity, is to look behind, and to return back.
144 = those who are in the faith of charity.
The Church then recedes successively from charity, and turns aside to faith... Signified. AC 3773:2.
These ideas surpass not only apprehension, but also faith.
Gerar = faith. AC 3368.
The state of the Lord as to the things which are of faith relatively to the rational things which were to be adjoined. Signified.

If truths Divine themselves were opened, they would not be received by those who are in the doctrinal things of faith, because they surpass all their rational apprehension, thus all their faith. Signified.
The man who... cannot do otherwise than profane, is withheld as far as possible from the acknowledgement and faith of truth and good.

They who are in the mere doctrinal things of faith, and not in the good of life, cannot but be in persuasive faith... But in proportion as anyone is in persuasive faith, he is stupid; but in proportion as anyone is in the good of life... he is in intelligence, that is, in faith from the Lord.

Conjunction is effected with those who... although they make faith the essential thing as to doctrine, still make charity the essential thing as to life; for with these there is confidence or trust in the Lord, which they call faith itself... Treated of. AC 3459. AC 3463.
Love and charity is spiritual conjunction, but not faith, except through love and charity.
That faith in the Lord would expire, according to the degrees in which charity would cease. Signified.
To kiss the Son = conjunction with Him through the faith of love.
States of faith are according to states of charity. Example(s).
When the order begins from love, everything which follows thence in genuine order appears flaming; but when the order begins from faith, everything... appears lucid...

The universal which Reuben signifies is faith. The reason faith is the first universal, is from the fact that when man is being regenerated... he must first learn and imbue the things which are of faith, that is, which are of spiritual truth...

Regarded in itself, faith is faith in the understanding and faith in the will; to know and to understand the truth which is of faith is called faith in the understanding; whereas to will the truth which is of faith is called faith in the will. Faith in the understanding is that which is signified by Reuben; and faith in the will is that which is signified by Simeon. That faith in the understanding, or the understanding of truth, precedes faith in the will, or the willing of truth, may be evident to everyone...

That to see, in the internal sense, = faith from the Lord, is evident from the fact, that the interior understanding has no other objects than the things which are of truth and good, for these are of faith. AC 3863:5, Illustrated.
To see God = to believe in Him, thus to see Him by faith; for they who are in faith, from faith see God; for God is in faith; and God is that in the faith which is truly faith.

To see = to have faith; for the Lord is seen only by faith; for faith is the eye of love; for by love through faith the Lord is seen; and love is the life of faith; and therefore it is said Ye shall see Me; because I live, ye shall live also.

(Thus) to see = faith from the Lord; for no other faith exists, which is faith, except that which is from the Lord; this, also, gives man to see, that is, to believe. But faith from self, or from the proprium of man, is not faith; for this causes him to see falsities as truths, and truths as falsities; and even if he sees truths as truths, still he does not see them, because he does not believe them; for he sees himself in them, and not the Lord.

The light of Heaven, being from the Lord, has with it intelligence and wisdom, consequently faith in Him; for faith in the Lord is within intelligence and wisdom; and therefore to see from that light... can signify nothing but faith in the Lord... It is this light which shines in the consciences of those who have faith in Him...

By faith, when it is distinguished from charity, is meant truth, such as is that of doctrine, or such as is contained in the confession which is called the Apostolic Faith; and this according to the general meaning of the word in the Church; for to have faith in truths is believed to be the faith by which there is salvation.
The state of faith if the will does not correspond to it. Signified.
The cardiac motions with them are according to the states of love; and the respiratory ones are according to the states of faith.
Under Cherub, see this reference.
Under Acknowledge, see this reference. AC 3906. AC 8694:3. AC 8882:2. AC 10205. AC 10218. AC 10370. DSS 58. DFaith 9. DFaith 11. DFaith 30. DFaith 30.
The truths of faith which are not learned for the sake of acting... are not of faith with him who learned them, but interiorly are against faith.
The twelve tribes = all things of faith and love. AC 3926. AC 3939:end.
The holy of faith. Signified.

The reason God hath judged me, and also hath heard my voice, in the internal sense, is the holy of faith, is that faith which is predicated of truth corresponds to the Divine justice... And the reason, why, in the external sense, it = the good of life, is (that) the holy of faith corresponds to the good of life.
They who reason about truth from... the negative, destroy all things of faith. Signified.
That they were in the negative as to all things of faith. Signified.
The works of faith, which from the appearance may also be called its fruits.
Under Confidence, see this reference. AC 4352:3. AC 4683:2. AC 4690:2. AC 5826:3. AC 5963:end. AC 6272:2. AC 9241. AC 9242:end. AC 9243.
Faith as to its state of love and charity. Signified.
They have not the truth of faith who believe that they have faith from self, thus are wise from self; but they have it who believe from the Lord; for to them faith and wisdom is given...
They had depended upon the faith of others...
Therefore man is in Heaven as to his interiors, when he is in spiritual love and faith.
Consequently, he acknowledges all things which confirm love and charity, which are called the things of faith...
The evil which a man has confirmed... even to faith and persuasion, cannot be amended.
Day = a state of faith or truth; and night, a state of no faith or truth.
The gentiles who have lived in mutual charity... in the other life receive faith more easily... than those within the Church who have not lived in such charity.
Seed = the faith of charity.
The inward quality of those who have only a scientific faith, shown.
He can confirm this by a number of his own experiences, if he is once in the faith that it is so.
The rock on which the Church will be built = the faith of charity.
With the spiritual man, this light falls into the things which are of faith with him... but with the celestial man, into the good of love.
Hence it was evident why they who lead a life of evil, can never, from a sincere heart, have faith in Divine truths...
Under every green tree = from the faith of all falsities.
Who took their lamps = ... faith in which is charity...

For he who is in the works of charity, or, what is the same, in the life of faith, is in the capacity of receiving faith, if not in the body, still in the other life; but he who is not in the works of charity... is in no capacity whatever of receiving faith, neither in the body, nor in the other life...
Every Church which commences from faith is such (as to quickly turn aside)... It has no other director than the understanding; and the understanding no other than that which is hereditary to man...
For faith is from Him through good.
Joseph's brethren = the things which are of faith; (for) they represent the Church which turns aside from charity to faith; and afterwards to faith separated from charity. AC 4721.
Those who were in faith, namely, in the faith of some charity. Signified.

The (ancients) did not know anything about faith, as the Christian Church does, but about Truth. Truth to them was the same as faith is to Christians; and in the Original Language there is the same word for both. AC 4765:end. AC 4769:3. AC 6180. DFaith 6. AR 111. AE 837:10.

But the Christian Church gives the name of faith to those doctrinal things which are the interiors of the Church, and are said to be what must be believed; for by faith the common people mean no other than the faith of creeds...
The brethren = those who teach from faith.
Those are said to fall from the general truth of the Church who acknowledge faith as essential, but not charity.
It treats of the Church which commences from faith, which from the very beginning it thus separates from charity...
But if the Church would acknowledge the life of faith as a principle, it would acknowledge charity towards the neighbour and love to the Lord, and hence the works of charity and love...
The Church which commences from faith would cease to be a Church, unless this Divine truth remained in it, that the Human of the Lord is Divine. Signified.
When (those who are in the affirmative) consult scientifics, they... corroborate faith...
That there was no longer any faith. Signified. AC 4765:end.
It cast Truth to the earth = that it cast down faith itself which in itself is charity; for faith regards charity, because it proceeds from charity.
Unless man is in the affection of good, and thence in faith in the Lord.

The sons by Tamar = the two essentials of the Church, namely, faith and love; Pharez, faith; and Zarah, love. Their birth represents that love is actually the first-born of the Church, and that faith is only apparently so.
For Er his first-born = the falsity of faith.
Unless there were light from good within man, he could never see truths to acknowledgement and faith.
To receive Divine truth is not only to have faith but also to act faith...
The reception of faith. Signified.

The case with faith is this. He that receives it, and that has it, is continually in the remembrance of the Lord, even when he is thinking or speaking about something else... for the remembrance of the Lord, on the part of those who are in faith, reigns universally...
The sphere of faith from charity is the sphere which reigns in Heaven...

The reception of faith is treated of, because the Sensuous, like the Rational, is re-born by faith, but by that faith into which charity flows; for unless charity flows into faith, and gives it life, faith cannot universally reign; since that reigns which a man loves...
When the faith of charity is the end... if there is correspondence, then faith from charity flows into the thought...
When faith is received in the exterior Natural... correspondence is effected, and charity is received... Treated of.
Hence from the life it may be known what is the quality of the faith; for good and evil are of the life, and truth and falsity are of the faith.
Therefore when there is no subordination (of the exterior Natural), a man cannot have any... faith.
Conjunction is effected by means of faith.
Beautiful in look = the things which are of faith... Spiritual look is faith. AC 5199:end, Explained.
This image, being interior, appears only to those who are in faith from charity.
Evil in look = the things which are not of faith.
Acknowledgement through faith, and adoration. Signified.

They who are in the affection of truth for the sake of truth and of life... have indeed faith in the doctrinal things of the Church; but still they search the Word... and thence have their faith and their conscience.
That all things of faith are thus conjoined together. Signified.
That faith in the will will be separated. Signified, Explained. AC 5482.
When there is faith in the will, truths become goods. Signified, Explained.
Under Confess, see this reference.
Destroying whatever is of faith.
To trust to scientifics in the things of faith, and not to have faith in any spiritual truth, unless what is scientific and sensuous dictates it. Signified.
Faith is corroborated by scientifics.

(Thus) what is scientific is by no means to be rejected from the truths of faith, but they are to be conjoined; by the prior way, however, that is, by the way from faith; and not by the posterior way, that is, by the way from scientifics.
Such have faith in those whom they believe to be enlightened.
How it is to be understood that through faith there is power in good, and the first power in truth. Explained, Signified.
Under Zebulon, see this reference.
At the beginning of regeneration, faith is in obscurity. Signified.
The Lord continually flows in through the internal of man with good and truth; the good gives life and its heat, which is love; and the truth gives enlightenment and its light, which is faith.
With those who are in... persuasive faith, the ideas of thought are exceedingly confined.
Chiding, because one wanted to destroy the faith of another. Signified.

Dost thou want to destroy my faith? Signified. Faith is of the Church; and these two things are so united, that he who destroys faith with anyone, destroys the Church with him; and this is to kill him; for he who takes away faith, takes away spiritual life.
That He endowed the Church with faith. Signified.
That if the Spiritual Church had not hope and faith they would be dragged down by falsities, evils, and profane things. Treated of. AC 6946. AC 6949. AC 6959.
Hence it is that no faith can ever be implanted in those of the Spiritual Church, unless with a mighty force they are withheld by the Lord from falsities. Signified, Explained.
That they may have faith concerning the Lord's Divine Human. Signified.

They who are of the Spiritual Church, in childhood, and afterwards in adolescence, have faith in the doctrinal things of their own Church; but at that time they have faith from their parents and masters, and not from themselves; and therefore if they afterwards recede from faith, they profane truth only slightly... Whereas if a man has faith in the doctrine of the Church and in the Word from himself, that is, by means of confirmations with himself, if he afterwards recedes... he profanes truth...
Providence, what would be the quality of those of the Spiritual Church if they had faith. Signified.

To have faith, here, does not mean faith from the signs... for this faith is concerned with worldly things; but faith, that if they do not remain in truths, they will become merely sensuous and corporeal, and at last profaners of truth... Faith in worldly things is quite different from faith in spiritual things. Example(s).
Light in the natural world corresponds to faith in the Spiritual World... and faith is actually the light of man.
That they did not receive from faith and obedience. Signified.

The Spiritual Church with man begins through faith in knowledge and afterwards in understanding, which is represented by Reuben and his sons. Afterwards, when the Church grows with man, that faith passes into the will, and from the will into act; and then the man wills the truth of faith, and does it, because it is so commanded in the Word. This [state] of faith is represented by Simeon. At last the affection of charity is perceived in his will, which is new, so that he wills to do good, not as before, from faith, but from charity towards the neighbour... This... is represented by Levi.
As the case is so with the Spiritual Church, it is not wonderful that with most, faith is the essential of the Church, and not charity.
That miracles contribute nothing to faith. Illustrated.

Pharaoh represents those who have professed faith, and have also persuaded themselves that faith saves, and yet have lived contrary to the precepts of faith; in a word, who have been in persuasive faith, and in a life of evil. Explained. (Their state in the other life.) AC 7418.
By these are meant those who have been in miraculous faith, and not in the faith of the Church.
In proportion as a man is in the loves of self and of the world... he does not know what faith is, until at last he does not know that it is anything.
In order that this Scientific may become of faith, it must be conjoined with good, and it then passes into the internal man, and becomes faith.
That which enters by an external way is perceived... Hence it is, that everything of the Church is attributed to faith.
It is the affections of truth and of good which constitute faith.
Everyone's faith is such as is his life. If, therefore, the life is damned, so is the faith; for when the life is evil it is the faith of falsity.
This persuasive is also supposed to be faith, but it is not faith; for it is impressed from the end that it may serve as a means for securing gain, honours, and reputation. Signified.
Who does not know... that it is the life of faith which makes man spiritual...

Every spiritual good proceeds either from faith, that is, through faith, or from love... He who is in the first state cannot enter into the second until he is regenerated; and he who is in the second state ought not to betake himself to the first... He relapses into the state of faith which had served to introduce him to good, and also beyond it. Signified.
The sacrifices = the worship of the Lord from faith; and the burnt-offerings... from love.
Faith is an internal affection, which consists in this, that a man wills from the heart to know what is true and what is good, not for the sake of doctrine, but for the sake of life.
It treats in () concerning faith in the Lord... Faith in the Lord is signified by the sanctification of the first-born. AC 8042.
When faith is mentioned, there is meant all the truth which is for the Spiritual Church... and therefore the Spiritual Church itself is meant...
When man is being regenerated, he is led by faith in the understanding or by doctrine, to faith in the will or life...
That which is (as it were) conceived in the womb, and born from the womb, is not man as man, but is the faith of charity; for this constitutes the Spiritual of man...
That faith merely natural is not to be ascribed to the Lord; but the truth of innocence which is therein. Signified, Explained. AC 8079.
The opening = that which is first born from a regenerate man, thus faith.

Faith merely natural is faith which is insinuated by an external way, and not by an internal one; as sensuous faith, which exists when a man believes that it is so, because the eye has seen it and the hand has touched it. (Signified by the Lord's words to Thomas). Also the faith of miracles, which exists when a man believes that it is so merely from miracles; and also the faith of authority, which exists when a man believes that it is so, because some one else, in whom he has faith, has said so. But spiritual faith is that which is insinuated by an internal and at the same time by an external way; insinuation by an internal way causes it to be believed, and then that which is insinuated by an external way causes it to be confirmed. The Spiritual of faith is the affection of charity, and thence the affection of truth for the sake of good use and for the sake of life; these cause faith to be spiritual. The insinuation of faith by an internal way is effected by the reading of the Word, and at the same time by enlightenment from the Lord, which is given according to the quality of the affection, that is, according to the end in the knowing of truth.
That the truths of faith are not to be ascribed to the Lord, but its goods. Signified.
For the Lord gives faith mediately by its good.
That therefore the faith of charity which is of the new generation, is to be ascribed to the Lord. Signified.

The falsities here signified by Pharaoh, etc. are chiefly the falsities of those who are in persuasive faith, that is, who persuade themselves that the doctrinal things of the Church in which they are, are true, and yet are in a life of evil. Persuasive faith exists together with evil of life, but not saving faith; for persuasive faith is a persuasion that all things which are of the doctrine of the Church are truths... for the sake of profits... and reputation. AC 9364.

Saving faith is given by the Lord; but (persuasive faith) is from the man himself; the former remains to eternity, the latter is dissipated in the other life: it is also dissipated in the world, if they gain nothing by it; but so long as they gain by it they light for it as if for Heaven itself... They who are in this faith in the world, can with difficulty be distinguished from those who are in saving faith; for they speak and preach in favour of what is doctrinal with an ardour as of zeal, but it is an ardour from the fire of the love of self and of the world... In the other life they are vastated as to this faith.
An endeavour to subjugate those who are in faith conjoined with charity. Signified.
To stand still and see = to have faith.
Trust is of love through faith; consequently, trust in... the Lord exists only with those who are in love to the Lord and towards the neighbour, because no others have faith.

That everything of faith and of the glory thence is from the Divine truth which is from Him. Signified. For all the glory which man has is from faith in the Lord; and thus the Lord is in faith, and therefore so is glory itself. (For) the Divine truth, from which and through which is faith, appears... as light.
In the other life everyone retains the principles of his faith which he had in the life of the body...

The interior (Angels of the Spiritual Kingdom) are those who are in charity itself, and thence in faith; but the exterior ones are those who are in faith, but not yet in charity: the latter do good from obedience; the former from affection.
The faith of the Lord's precepts. Signified.
He who leads a life of faith performs repentance daily...
No faith, and consequently no obedience. Signified.
Rock = faith, here, faith from the Lord, or the Lord as to faith. Illustrated.

The reason (the power of opening and shutting Heaven and Hell) belongs to faith, is that faith is from the Lord, thus also is of the Lord, that is, the Lord Himself is in it: all power in the other life is through the truth of faith from good.
The faith which is from the Lord is from the Divine law, that is, from the Word; for by means of this the Lord teaches what faith is, and also gives faith.
Faith is given through truths, and, in fact, through the primary ones; for enlightenment is effected from these...
When Moses lifted up his hand = when faith with those of the Spiritual Church looked to the Lord.
As spiritual power is faith...
When he let down his hand = when faith with them looked downwards, or from the Lord to self and the world.
The reason the faith which looks to the Lord conquers, is that the Lord then lights; for the Lord is faith, because faith is from Him...
They who are of the Spiritual Church cannot be in faith which continually looks to the Lord; but are alternately in faith which looks to self and the world. Signified.
They who have used knowledges as a means to annihilate the things which are of faith, have utterly destroyed their Intellectual...
He who does not know that the Lord is the Saviour of the world, cannot have faith in Him...
(Thus) the life of the regenerate man is the life of faith.
Faith in act. Signified.
Action from the light of intelligence, thus from for faith from the Lord is in the light of intelligence. Signified.
Truth = faith.
Hence there is a correspondence... of light in the world with faith, which is thence called spiritual light.
They who believe... that the essential of worship is the life of faith, that is, charity towards the neighbour and love to the Lord, belong to the internal Church.
They belong to the external Church who do good to the neighbour and worship the Lord solely from the obedience of faith...
The eagle, here, = faith.
The dove = faith.
Love to God and love towards the neighbour... can exist only by means of faith.
That there may be a permanent faith of truth. Signified.
A veiling over of the interiors so that they may appear in the holy of faith... Signified.
For there to be a Church there must be with the man of the Church faith in the Lord, and also love to Him and love towards the neighbour.
The obscurity of faith, such as that of those of the Spiritual Church... Signified.

In order that truths may be of faith... they flow in from the Lord... When they are taken out of the memory, and through the Intellectual are insinuated into the will... and thence into act, they become living, and are of faith. This is effected by the Lord when the man desists from evils.
They who find the delight of life in adulteries can no longer receive anything of faith...
The eye corresponds to faith; the left eye to the truth of faith, and the right eye to the good of faith; in the opposite sense, to the evil which is of faith.
The state of faith with everyone. Signified.

The Church at this day is predicated and so called from faith... and few know what faith is. Most believe that faith is to know those things which the doctrine of the Church teaches, and to be persuaded that they are truths; but not that it is to live according to them... But the learned believe that that faith is confidence or trust that they are saved by the Lord having suffered for them... Love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour is the very being of Heaven and the Church, and faith is the manifesting thence.
Not to those who are not from the faith of the Church. Signified, Explained.
A weak state as to the faith of truth. Signified.
Passages in the Word where faith is mentioned, and not love. Explained.
Man has his spiritual life through faith from the Word.

That which has become of the faith of anyone, even if not true, is not to be rejected, except by a full view. If it is done sooner, the initiament of his spiritual life is extirpated. Example(s), Signified.

Heart = the life of love; soul, the life of faith... To the will appertains love... to the understanding appertains faith. When these two lives of man are one, the things which are of faith are also of love, for they are loved; and, on the other hand, the things which are of love are also of faith, because they are believed.
They who are in faith in the Lord, and thence in charity towards the neighbour, constitute the province of the lungs.

The reason faith appertains to the intellectual faculty, is that this is enlightened by the Lord when the man receives faith; hence, when he is reading the Word, he has light... in such things as are of faith.

For faith without love is not faith, and love without faith is not love; for love has its quality from faith, and faith has its life from love; hence faith without love is dead, and faith with love is alive.
In the Word where faith is treated of, love is also treated of.
Soul, here = the life of faith, and therefore faith itself with a man, because this constitutes his spiritual life.
It is the interior understanding which is enlightened by the Lord when a man receives faith; for this is in the light of Heaven, and in this is the spiritual life of man...
This is by faith to serve the Lord, and by love the world... Signified.
Let those who are sensuous remain in their own faith, provided they believe that...
A vine = faith in the Lord; thus it = the Lord as to faith; for the Lord is faith, because faith is from Him; for faith is not faith, except that which is from Him.

The fire of life is man's love, and the light of life is his faith... The love of truth and the faith of truth constitute the light of life with a good man and an Angel... and the love of falsity and the faith of falsity constitute the lumen of life with an evil man and a Spirit of Hell. AC 9637:end.
The goods of the Church are the being and soul of faith; for from them faith is faith, and lives.
Truths once made of faith... cannot be eradicated, and the falsities which afterwards become of faith conjoin themselves with them.

That all things of faith also, which are by them, are to be ascribed to the Lord. Signified. All things of faith, which are signified by the first-born sons, are those which are from the good of charity; for faith comes forth from this good. For truths, whether taken from the Word or the doctrine of the Church, cannot possibly become of faith, unless there is good in which they may be implanted. Explained. Therefore he who supposes that faith is faith with man, before he wills these truths, and from willing does them, is very much mistaken... Truth becomes good, or faith charity, in the will.
On the doctrine of charity and of faith. General article. AC 9363. AC 9443. AC 9585. AC 9701. AC 9796. AC 9974. AC 10167. AC 10318. AC 10386. AC 10519. AC 10591. AC 10714, etc.
That those only are in faith who live according to the precepts of faith, the Lord teaches in . To come to the light = to come to faith in the Lord, thus to faith from the Lord.

In the second state (of regeneration) goods... go forth out of Heaven through the will into the Intellectual, and there appear in the form of faith. It is this faith which is saving, because it is from the good of love, that is, through the good of love from the Lord; for this faith is charity in form.
See Affection of good.
Truths from good are the truths of faith, because faith is of good.
(Thus) persuasive faith is a faith of the lips and not of the heart.

They who are in persuasive faith do not know from any internal enlightenment whether it is truths or falsities which they are teaching; nay, they do not care, provided they are believed by the common people; for they are in no affection of truth for the sake of truth. They also defend faith alone more than others, and only make any account of the good of faith, which is charity, in proportion as they can make profit by it.

They who are in persuasive faith recede from faith if they are deprived of honours and gains, provided their reputation is not endangered; for persuasive faith is not within man, but stands outside, being in the memory alone, from which it is taken out when it is being taught; and therefore this faith together with ite truths vanishes away after death; for there then remains only that of faith which is within man, that is, which is rooted in good, thus which has become of the life. AC 10182:5.
They who are in persuasive faith, are meant by these passages in Matthew. Illustrated.
They saw God = faith.
Then at the same time the Lord Hows in with faith, by means of the cooperation of the new will...

Love is like a fire... and faith is like the light from that fire... and also is a light which illuminates the interiors of his understanding. Hence it is evident what is the quality of the light from which is the faith with those who are in infernal love. That from this light comes persuasive faith, which in itself is not faith, but a persuasion that it is so for the sake of self and the world, see above.
It is more easy to make a raven white than to make those believe who have once at heart rejected faith. But let these things... be for those few who are in faith.
The eye, here, = faith and the intelligence thence.
In the middle Heaven there is conjunction with the Lord through faith implanted in the good of charity towards the neighbour.
A stone like a mill-stone = the truth through which there is faith.
The light received is faith. But... faith is not a lamp, and does not illuminate the mind, unless it is from charity, thus unless it is charity...
They who are in the Celestial Kingdom do not know truths from knowledge and the faith thence, but from internal perception.
In Heaven, love is the end of all things of the will, and faith is the end of all things of the thoughts.
Thou shalt make coats = the things which are of faith... The proceeding from the Spiritual which is from the Celestial is that which is called the faith of truth.
For the faith which looks to good from self, and not from God, is not true faith...
As man is ignorant of this, he attributes everything of salvation to faith, and scarcely anything to charity, when yet faith has its being from charity...

When Heaven is closed, there does indeed exist the knowledge of the truths of faith... but never faith which is faith; for the faith which is faith comes from above, that is, through Heaven from the Lord.

The things which are of love are perceived as goods, and the things which are of faith are perceived as truths. Even falsities are of faith, and evils are of love, with those who are in falsities and evils.
Life from the Divine is given through faith, the first of which is acknowledgement.

It was frequently said by the Lord, when the sick were being healed, that they should have faith, and that it should be unto them according to their faith. Illustrated. The reason was, that the first thing of all is to acknowledge that the Lord is the Saviour of the world... AE 815:3. Ath 16. Ath 64. Ath 204. Ath 213.
Without the good of innocence, there does not exist... faith which has life in it.
To do according to the Lord's precepts... is truly love and truly faith.
It pleases the Lord that man should have strength through faith from love, as to those things which are of his spirit...
The faith of everyone is as his love. Explained.

The third state is called the state of intelligence... At this time faith commences; for faith is not the faith of the man himself until he has confirmed that which he believes by the ideas of his Own thought. Before this, faith is not his, but is of another in him; for he has believed in the person and not in the thing.
To represent all things of faith serving the good of love. Signified.
Unless faith is conjoined with love it is neither faith nor love there for faith is truth.
Eyes... = faith which is seen and perceived.
A state of faith in God. Signified.
That a rock = faith, is from the appearances in the other life; they who are in faith dwell there upon rocks.
What is obscure and false of faith. Signified.
What is scientific made persuasive, they call faith.
The faith of truth and the love of good conjoin man with the Lord; and the faith of falsity and the love of evil conjoin man with Hell.
They who are in the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom worship Him from faith...
Many suppose that they worship the Lord through faith, when they believe the things which are of the doctrine of the Church...
The Lord inflows into the life of man, and thence into the faith...

There are two things which make the life of man, love and faith; love the life of his will, and faith the life of his understanding. Hence such as is the love, and such as is the faith, such is the life.
The love of good and the faith of truth thence make the life of Heaven; and the love of evil and the faith of falsity thence make the life of Hell.
Heaven exists with everyone according to the reception of love and faith from the Lord.
Love to the Lord and love towards the neighbour make Heaven, and also faith; but the latter only in proportion as it has life from those loves.
The external Church exists with those who do the Lord's precepts from faith; for these are they who believe in the Lord.

They confuse (those of the Sixth Earth) by saying that they ought to have faith... But they answered them, that they do not know what faith is... because they perceive in themselves that it is so. For they were of the Lord's Celestial Kingdom... SE 5513:3.
They who receive truths first in the memory, then in the understanding, and at last in the will, are they who are in faith; for they act from faith, which is then called conscience.
That at the end of the Church, when there is no longer love, and consequently no longer faith, the Lord will open the Word as to its internal sense. Signified.
That a Divine which is not perceivable by any idea is not receptible in faith. References.
In the Spiritual Kingdom there is... charity; and the light of truth thence is intelligence, which is also called faith.
The Lord is present with everyone according to the love and the faith.

When a man is such, the things which he thinks from the understanding are of his faith, and the things which he thinks from the will are of his love; and therefore with him, faith and love conjoin themselves, like the understanding and the will.
For whether you say the faith, or the determinate thought of man, it is the same; for what a man believes, he also thinks.
Love makes the man, and faith only so far as it proceeds from love; and deeds or works proceed from both.
Faith is the affection of truth proceeding from heavenly love which is from the Lord. HH 482.

That faith does not remain if it is not from heavenly love. General article... There is no faith at all, neither can any exist, with those who are in corporeal and worldly love (alone); it is only knowledge, or the persuasion that it is true because it serves their love. A number of those who supposed that they were in faith were brought to those who were in faith, and communication having been given, they perceived that they had no faith at all. They also afterwards confessed that merely to believe the truth and the Word is not faith, but to love truth from heavenly love, and to will and do it from interior affection. It was also shown, that their persuasion, which they called faith, was only like the light of winter... And therefore the light of the persuasive faith with them, the moment it is touched by the rays of the light of Heaven... becomes dense darkness. LJ 37. DLife 49. DP 170.
It comes to the same thing whether you say truth or faith, because faith is of truth and truth is of faith. References. DLife 43.
On faith. General article.
Faith enters man, and becomes his, when he wills and loves that which he knows and perceives; meanwhile it is outside of him.
Faith is not faith with man unless it becomes spiritual; and it is not spiritual unless it becomes of love; and it becomes of love when a man loves to live truth and good...
Faith is the affection of truth from willing truth because it is truth; and to will truth because it is truth is the Spiritual itself of man... LJ 36.
(References to passages on the subject of faith.) LJ 39.
Faith in impossibilities has no existence; that is, faith in such things as a man thinks are impossibilities.
Mere believing is not faith; but to will and do that which is believed is faith.
The understanding is the receptacle of faith.
That at this day faith within the Church is so rare, that it can scarcely be said there is any...
They said that at this day interior Divine truths are revealed among that nation, and that they are received in spiritual faith, that is, in life and heart.
In the western quarter (of that London) dwell those who profess faith.
Man ought to shun evils and do good as of himself, yet with the acknowledgement that it is from the Lord; and there is no faith before, and still less that thought which he calls faith.

There is the faith of God, and there is the faith of man; they have the faith of God who perform repentance; but they have the faith of man who do not perform repentance, and still think about imputation; and the faith of God is living faith, and the faith of man is dead faith.
From the love of truth proceeds the perception of truth; from the perception of truth the thought of truth; and from these comes the acknowledgement of truth, which is faith in its own genuine sense.
That in so far as anyone shuns evils as sins, he has faith. General article.
Faith and life are distinguished from each other as are thinking and doing; (thus) as are the understanding and the will.

As it is of faith to know and think, and still more to understand that it is so, it is possible for a man to believe that he has faith, and yet not have it. The reason he has it not, is that he is in evil of life...
Thus is effected the conjunction of faith and life...
He who does not shun evils as sins has no faith because he is in evil, and evil inwardly hates truth...
The faith of an evil man is intellectual faith, in which there is nothing of good from the will; thus it is dead faith. (Described by comparisons.)
Very different is faith in the understanding in which there is good from the will...
There are many things which appear to be of faith only. Enumerated. DLife 48, Explained.
Hence it may be seen what is spiritual faith, and what is faith not spiritual; and that spiritual faith exists with those who do not commit sins...
(Thus) there does not exist with man a grain of faith more than there is of life... but faith and life march on with equal step.
If there were not reception by man, and then thought as from himself, nothing could have been said about faith; for faith is not from man.
(Title). The Doctrine of the New Jerusalem concerning Faith.
That faith is the internal acknowledgement of truth. General article.

At this day, by faith nothing else is meant than thought that it is so because the Church so teaches, and because it is not evident before the understanding. For it is said, Believe, and do not doubt. If you answer, I do not comprehend, it is said that therefore it is to be believed. So that modern faith is the faith of what is unknown, and may be called blind faith; and as it is the dictate of one person in another, it is historical faith.

Real faith is nothing else than the acknowledgement that it is so because it is true. For he who is in real faith thinks and speaks thus, This is true, and therefore I believe it; for faith is of truth, and truth is of faith...
As the Angels are in (the spiritual affection of truth) they utterly reject the dogma that the understanding is to be under obedience to faith...
(Thus) faith and Truth are one...

The reason faith is mentioned by the Lord... was that the Jews did not believe... that the Lord was the Messiah... and when truth is not believed, faith is mentioned. Still, it is one thing to have faith and believe in the Lord, and another to have faith and believe in some one else.
Faith separated from Truth entered and invaded the Church together with the papal dominion, because the chief security of that religion was ignorance of truth.
Blind faith also remained afterwards with many of the Reformed, because they separated faith from charity...

If anyone should say... How can I have the internal acknowledgement of truth which is faith? I cannot: I will tell him how he can. Shun evils as sins, and approach the Lord, and you will have as much as you desire.

This storehouse (of Knowledges) is in the highest degree necessary, because without it faith cannot be formed; for the Knowledges of truth and good enter into faith and make it. If there are none, faith does not come forth; for a faith void and empty has no existence. If they are few, the faith is scanty and needy; if they are many, the faith is rich and full according to the abundance of them. DFaith 29:end.
It is (however) the Knowledges of genuine truth and good which make faith, and not at all the Knowledges of falsity; for faith is Truth; and falsity, being opposite to Truth, destroys faith.

The Knowledges of truth and good which precede faith appear to some to be of faith; but still they are not... They are only of the thought that it is so... And the faith that they are Truths, while it is not known that they are so, is a kind of persuasion remote from internal acknowledgement. The moment, however, that charity is implanted, these Knowledges become of faith, but no further than charity is in that faith.
He then becomes truly a man... of whom charity makes the life, and faith the form, which is beautiful according to the quality thereof; but his faith is then no longer called faith, but intelligence.
The Christian faith in a universal idea. General article. AR 67. BE 116. TCR 2. TCR 121:3.
The modern faith in a universal idea. General article.
Faith in its essence is Truth, and Truth is manifold.
They who are in spiritual love... have intelligence (inscribed on their life)... Neither do these know what faith is. If faith is mentioned they understand Truth.

But they who are in spiritual natural love have neither wisdom nor intelligence inscribed on their life, but they have somewhat of faith from the Word, in so far as this somewhat is conjoined with charity...

But they who have confirmed themselves in faith in what is unknown, and at the same time have been in some affection of truth, are instructed by the Angels according to their reception of Truths, and a life according to them...
Without this appearance there cannot be... faith.

(Thus) the faith induced by miracles is not faith, but persuasion; for there is nothing rational in it, still less anything spiritual... It is the same with everything a man does from this persuasive faith... For a miracle infuses faith by an external way, and not by an internal way; thus from the world, and not from Heaven; and the Lord enters man solely by an internal way, which is through the Word...
It is therefore vain to think that anyone can... receive any faith during sickness; for... in that faith there is no charity...

From interior enlightenment from the Lord, a rational man at the first hearing perceives... that love is the life of faith, or that faith lives from love... Again, that whatever a man believes from love, he also wills and does, and therefore that to have faith is also to do; and also that a wicked man cannot have the love of God, and thus cannot have the faith of God.
There is also another kind of enlightenment, by which it is revealed to man in what faith he is...
The internal faith conquers with those who acknowledge God at heart; but the external faith with these who do not acknowledge God at heart, however they may with the lips.
Charity does not exist without faith.
The faith that man does not live after death...
V. (The Roman Catholic doctrine of faith.) BE 5. BE 23.
3a. (The Reformed doctrine of faith.)
(Predictions from the Lord concerning Himself and His Church) for those who are in faith from charity, or in truths of wisdom from the good of love. Signified.
Thou hast not denied My faith () = that they acknowledge the Word, that it is Divine Truth. ( = constancy in truths. AE 136.)

To the Angel in the Church of Thyatira write = to those and concerning those who are in faith from charity, and thence in good works; and also to those and concerning those who are in faith separated from charity, and thence in evil works.
(I know) thy faith () = the Truth. AE 155.
The Angels said, What is faith without light?
At this day, instead of... intelligence they say faith. AR 420.
That everything living of faith has perished. Signified.

The Angel cried to the flock of sheep, Do not listen to them. They have not receded from their former faith... which faith is not faith in the Lord. Neither is faith a tree; but man. But do repentance, and look to the Lord, and you will have faith; faith before this is not a faith in which there is anything living.
The works which (they call) the fruits of faith, are invisible, done within the man by the Holy Spirit, of which the man knows nothing...
